title: Travel & places
text:
Niagara Falls
FIELD NOTES / A DIFFERENT PACE
Some places make it easier to slow down and pay attention. Here, the movement of the water and the scale of the landscape are a reminder to look beyond the frame of a photograph.
I’m interested in the small details that make a place feel different: how people move through it, where they gather, and what they stop to notice.

title: What a chart can tell me
text: A chart makes some patterns easier to see, but it also reflects a series of choices. Which observations belong in the plot? What belongs on each axis? Which differences deserve attention?

title: What a chart can tell me
text:
One choice that matters
In a comparison of income and life expectancy, a logarithmic income axis changes the spacing of the values. That can help reveal patterns that are difficult to see when a few large values stretch the scale.

title: What a chart can tell me
section: What I still need to ask
text:
What I still need to ask
A visible association does not explain why the pattern exists. Before moving from description to explanation, I need to think about the research question, the data, and possible alternative explanations.
My next step is to describe the plot in one careful sentence, then write down a question it cannot answer.

title: Home
text:
STUDENT / RESEARCHER / EXPLORER


Making sense of the social world.
I am an undergraduate student deeply interested in the politics of the Middle East and North Africa, with a focus on how states in the region develop politically and economically. My studies explore the relationship between government institutions, economic systems, and patterns of development, as well as how regional and global dynamics influence domestic politics. I am particularly drawn to understanding the challenges of governance, reform, and economic diversification across MENA states.

title: A place to keep my questions
text:
This website begins with a simple idea: make a little space for work that is still taking shape.
Not every post needs to be a finished argument. I want to use this notebook to explain something I’ve learned, record a question that stayed with me, or connect an idea from class to something I noticed elsewhere.

title: A place to keep my questions
text:
What I’ll write about
I expect to share reflections on course projects, small discoveries while learning R, and observations from places I visit. Over time, these notes should show how my questions change.

title: Academic interests & research
text:
I’m interested in the politics and political economy of the Middle East and North Africa, particularly how states in the region develop politically and economically.

Governance and reform: How do political institutions shape reform and development across MENA states?
Economic diversification: How are states working to reduce their dependence on traditional sources of revenue and develop new sectors?
Regional and global politics: How do international and regional dynamics influence domestic politics and economic development?
Data and political analysis: How can quantitative data help us better understand political and economic patterns across countries?
Political participation: Who gets involved, and what makes participation easier?
Cities and communities: How do local environments shape everyday choices?
Data and communication: How can a chart make a complex pattern easier to understand?

text:
A project I’m developing

Oil Rents and Inequality in the Middle East and North Africa
I am examining the relationship between oil rents and economic inequality across MENA countries using quantitative data and regression analysis.


Economic Diversification in the Gulf
I am interested in how Gulf states are responding to economic and geopolitical change through diversification, and how political institutions influence these efforts.


Data Analysis in Political Science
I am developing my skills in R, RStudio, GIS, and computational methods to study political and economic questions using empirical data.
